newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr opens stronger ahead of Ontario budget.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr opens stronger ahead of Ontario budget.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3771 (US$0.7261) in light trading on Tuesday after some overnight corporate interest to buy the unit on overseas markets, traders said. * They said the currency's strength was based on a decline in interest rate speculation and expectations that the Province of Ontario will release a market-friendly budget later today.

Economists have predicted that Ontario's 1996/97 deficit would drop below C$7.0 billion and some have said the provincial government could wipe out its deficit by fiscal 1999/2000, one year ahead of plan.
The provincial government has delivered 15 percent of a promised 30 percent tax cut by 1999, and some economists speculated another 15 percent could be offered in this latest budget.
"There's a strong suspicion that the Ontario budget numbers are going to be better than expected," one trader said.
The Canada dollar also has benefited from growing sentiment that the U.S. Federal Reserve would not raise interest rates at its May 20 meeting.
The Fed last raised rates 25 basis points on March 25, a move that led to a subsequent sell-off of the Canadian dollar.
Michael Gregory, strategist and economist with Lehman Brothers, said he expected the dollar would be hard-pressed to strengthen past the C$1.3700 (US$0.7299) level in the next two weeks.
"The Canadian dollar, as we move on ahead here, is probably going to stall," Gregory said.
The Canadian dollar has gained back almost 50 percent of its value lost since the last Fed hike in March.
The federal election, which usually brings some volatility to the markets, effectively rules out any further large gains by the currency, Gregory said.
Overseas, the British pound strengthened against the major currencies, including the Canadian dollar, on the back of a 25-basis-point hike by the Bank of England.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2572 marks from Monday's close of 1.2563 and dipped to 91.20 yen from Monday's 91.72 yen.
